title: Paramedic Trainees' Clinical Placement in Maternity Units (ParaPlace-Mat): a Germany-wide online survey to evaluate the obstetrics placement from the learners’ perspective and to assess their clinical confidence
summary:
As part of the training to become a paramedic, in accordance with the Training and Examination Regulations for Paramedics (NotSan-APrV, Annex 3, paragraph 5), a 40-hour placement in paediatrics and obstetrics must be completed. This can be undertaken in an obstetrics, paediatrics or paediatric surgery department, intensive care unit or ward with relevant patients. Little is currently known about how the placement is actually carried out. However, this placement could provide valuable practical experience in paediatrics and obstetrics, helping to ensure better preparation for such cases in the emergency medical services.
It is important that paramedics are able to provide assistance confidently and calmly, as an unplanned birth taking place outside a hospital poses risks to both the mother and the child.
Studies show that many emergency medical service staff feel uncertain when attending births. They often have little practical experience, even though the training programme includes a placement in paediatrics and obstetrics. How these placements are to be carried out exactly is not clearly defined.

interventions.name: Participants fill out a questionnaire. It takes about 20 minutes to complete.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Paramedics and trainee paramedics who have completed their paediatric and obstetric placement and who are currently undertaking or have completed their paramedic training in a German federal state; informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Paramedics who passed their state examination before 2024; withdrawal of consent.
